claims.description: THR-SPLIT E3. Replaces privacy-lint-{user-paths,vault-name,worker-repo-names,model-id}, which demanded zero occurrences over the whole tracked tree minus four hand-written pathspec exclusions. That claim was unsatisfiable twice over and unverified once: the rule that removes a string must state the string (scripts/path_transform_rule_v1.json), evidence fixed by a digest cannot be edited without breaking the digest that fixes it, and nothing checked that an exclusion was entitled to be one -- docs/adrs/ was excluded wholesale and is where nearly the whole real exposure lives (measured: runs/THR-SPLIT/20260816T013706Z/ESITO-1-what-is-already-public.md). The reformulation: ZERO on the surface a change ADDS (every tracked file whose bytes differ from the declared baseline), EXACTLY the declared count on the surface that already exists (==, not <=, so a public file that grows an occurrence turns this red), and exactly two machine-checkable exemption reasons -- the file is a rule that names what it replaces (hits confined to its own pattern/replacement slots, or, for this declaration itself, each hit being exactly a declared literal), or the file is evidence whose sha256 is pinned by another tracked file. A file in neither is not an exemption. Two classes -- the operator's home path and this host's name -- are COMPUTED from the running process and never written down, so no declaration can name them and none can launder them; that asymmetry is what stops this declaration from becoming the hand-written exclusion it replaces. The --selftest arm is the non-vacuity guard: eleven scratch repositories, each judged as intended, on every run. The last two are the separation itself -- one tree measured twice, differing only in whether it has a remote: a repository with no remote has no public surface, and the day the internal surface gains one, this claim stops being satisfied by emptiness and names what would travel. tests/bypass_ft_internal_enters_public_surface_fixture.sh drives the same boundary independently, and was observed RED with each exemption reason disabled before it was observed green.

Until 2026-08-19 the pattern was anchored with the word-boundary escape under git grep -E, whose ERE engine does not implement that escape: the predicate matched zero lines by construction and could not fail. Corrected to -P and measured at correction time on the tracked tree: RED, 212 lines across 41 files -- 211 lines in 40 files under runs/THR-SUBAGENT/, 1 line in 1 file under .verity/evidence/. Declared RED as observed, the same discipline the falsifier register applies to a known red (the bypass_ft_bash_unbound and FT-28 rows): this claim is expected to stay RED until the operator records a decision on the exposure it now measures, and a GREEN here means the exposure left the tracked surface. It is declared and not repaired because the repair is not this claim's to take: three of the carrying files are cited by sha256 from tracked conformance records that resolve today, and the order of redaction and re-pinning is an operator decision. 2026-09-04, operator acceptance. The 212 lines across 41 files split along the pin structure, which is why the repair costs one commit and no re-pinning: 211 lines in 40 files under runs/THR-SUBAGENT/ leave this claim's perimeter through a fifth pathspec exclusion, and the one carrier outside that tree -- .verity/evidence/2026-08-01-adr008-testrun/adr008-tmpdir-probe.txt, 1 line -- is redacted at the tip. Those 40 are exactly the carriers fixed by sha256 from tracked records (49 carrier-record-line pairs: 40 rows in INTEGRITY.md, 9 rows across six files under runs/THR-CONFORMANCE/20260814T002404Z/records/), and the redacted one is exactly the carrier no tracked record pins, so no digest goes stale and no second commit is owed. What this GREEN does not say is that the exposure is gone: all 41 files and all 212 lines are already at origin/main, redaction at the tip changes what a fresh clone shows and does not unpublish, and the 40 excluded files keep their 211 lines on the tracked surface. The exclusion states the perimeter in which this rule is applicable -- the tracked surface minus runs/THR-SUBAGENT/ and the four earlier exclusions -- and it was observed refusing before it was accepted: a bare token seeded into a tracked path inside the perimeter turns this claim RED and names that path, while the same token inside runs/THR-SUBAGENT/ does not. An exclusion never seen to refuse would be the vacuous green ADR-018 D3 names at :470-471, and this one is not.

ADR-020 D3: every emitted in-toto Statement conforms to D2's allowlist. Unlike the privacy-lint claims above, this one presides over the EMITTED ARTIFACT and not over the tree -- side-car Statements are written beside the receipt under an ignored directory, so no git grep can ever reach them, which is the defect ADR-020 D1 measured in privacy-lint-user-paths. The --selftest arm is the control: it requires the boundary to accept a conforming specimen and refuse five leaking ones on every run, so the claim still discriminates on a checkout where no run has emitted anything yet. tests/bypass_att_prose_leak_fixture.sh drives the same detector with more arms.

DECLARED RED, and RED because observed RED on the tree that installs it -- not a target, a measurement. WHAT IS MEASURED IS ONE DIRECTION: the tracked corpus of conformance records read against scripts/conformance_verify.py, and the keysets that verifier declares closed. NOT A ROUND-TRIP, and this claim's earlier id asserted one -- the tracked emitter scripts/conformance_record.py writes `transformation` as None (line 236) and no tracked program writes `completeness` into it, so the refused records have no tracked producer and no emitter-to-verifier loop is under measurement. The three tracked records under runs/THR-CONFORMANCE/20260814T002404Z/records/ carry `completeness` inside `transformation`, whose closed keyset the verifier declares to be {id, sha256} exactly; all three verify NOT-RECOMPUTABLE naming that key. The verifier refuses this repository's own evidence, in the tracked tree and not only on a clone. The falsifier resolves all three legs BY CONTENT and never by filename: the verifier is the tracked module declaring a closed keyset for `transformation`, an emitter is a tracked module declaring the same PREDICATE_TYPE and no keyset of its own, and the corpus is every tracked file whose top-level predicateType matches -- read statically, nothing imported and nothing executed. FOUR OUTCOMES, NEVER TWO: hits>0 on a populated corpus is RED (1), hits=0 on a populated corpus is GREEN (0), a corpus that is empty or did not resolve is UNMEASURED (2), and an emitter that was not located is UNMEASURED (3) -- an exit shared between green and unmeasured reports a vacuum as a pass, which is the defect this judge refuses to reproduce. The GREEN arms are non-vacuous BY GENERATION, not by grep: twelve generated records carrying no out-of-vocabulary key answer GREEN over a printed corpus count of twelve, and the same twelve with one mutated answer RED on exactly one hit. This claim expects exit 1 and the falsifier's own verdict line, so a run that goes red for some other reason does not satisfy it, and the repair -- widening the keyset or moving the records, whose digests three sibling narrowing.json files pin -- is the edit that must flip this row to 0.

claims.description: DECLARED UNMEASURED-BASELINE, and observed so: INTEGRITY.md, the baseline file this gate reads, exists in the commit that installs the gate and carries no such section. The claim measures SET IDENTITY -- the set of unattributed commits reachable from HEAD must EQUAL, member for member, a set declared by enumeration in INTEGRITY.md, which is the only tracked integrity declaration this repository has -- a second declaration file at the root would be a second door on the same room. A PRESENT FILE WITH NO SECTION IS NOT AN EMPTY ENUMERATION, and arm B-nosection holds the two apart while arm B-empty reads the empty declaration out of the byte-identical file arm A reads a true one from. The enumeration is `.git-blame-ignore-revs`-shaped: one full sha per line, '#' at the start of a line for a comment, free text after the sha ignored, so the declaration carries each commit's date and subject beside it and stays a machine-read set. A COMMENT IS NOT A DECLARATION -- arm C-commented-out comments out a true member and requires RED. Never a cardinality: a declared superset is RED, a declared subset is RED, and a baseline that swaps one member for another is RED at unchanged cardinality -- the fixture's arm S exists to prove that, because a gate comparing two counts would pass it. SCOPE IS HEAD-REACHABLE and not origin/main..HEAD: after a push origin/main moves, and a gate scoped to the unpushed range would stop measuring every commit it had just published. THE CLASSIFICATION IS DERIVED, not asserted: the judge reads %G? for every commit and prints the distribution and the map before applying it. G and U are the SAME ATTRIBUTED class, because gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile lives outside the repository and a clone without it reads U where this host reads G -- measured at this basis as 173 G + 18 N here and 173 U + 18 N with that setting blinded, the N set identical across the two. N is the unattributed class; B, E, X, Y and R are absent from this tree and are deliberately unbucketed, so an unclassified code halts the fixture rather than being folded silently into either side. THE KEY IS THE SHA, WITH THE PATCH-ID AS FALLBACK: a declared sha absent from the observed set but whose stable patch-id matches an observed unattributed commit stays exempt and prints STALE-SHA, so a rebase does not re-accuse an accepted commit; a declared sha no object answers to is BOGUS and RED; and one that resolves by neither is UNMEASURED-STALE (6), neither green nor red. SIX EXITS, none shared between GREEN and a non-measurement: 0 GREEN, 1 RED, 2 UNMEASURED-SCOPE, 3 UNMEASURED-BASELINE, 6 UNMEASURED-STALE, 4 FIXTURE BROKEN. This claim expects 3 AND the judge's own verdict line, so a run that fails to reach its question for some other reason does not satisfy it. The edit that flips this row to 0 is the commit that writes the INTEGRITY.md section and argues the acceptance there.
